title: Exciton Diffusion Drives Efficiency Roll-off in TADF OLEDs
authors: Liam G. King; Arvydas Ruseckas; Tao Wang; Subeesh Madayanad Suresh; Eli Zysman-Colman; Ifor D.W. Samuel
abstract: 2 Abstract Despite their potential to deliver high-efficiency organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), those using thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF) emitters often suffer from a large drop in efficiency at high luminance. This effect is known as efficiency roll-off and is a longstanding issue for these devices, which has limited their commercial deployment. We have discovered that the degree of overlap between the photoluminescence (PL) and absorption spectra drives singlet exciton diffusion and is a strong predictor of the magnitude of efficiency roll-off in TADF OLEDs. This effect is especially important in OLEDs made with multiresonant (MR)-TADF materials given their intense low-energy short-range charge transfer absorption bands. MR-TADF OLEDs are very appealing due to their narrow emission spectra; however, their small Stokes shift leads to large spectral overlap and contributes to these devices showing severe efficiency roll-off. Developing TADF materials that have a larger Stokes shift whilst maintaining their bright, narrow emission would help minimize efficiency roll-off while securing high internal quantum efficiencies, features particularly relevant for displays.

title: Transglutaminase-Crosslinked Collagen Gel Delays Gastrointestinal Transit and Prolongs Serum Appearance of Antioxidant Collagen Di- and Tripeptides in Mice
authors: Yapeng Lu; Ying He; Xin Feng; Mi Yan; Yexing Liang; Liang Ma; Yuhao Zhang
abstract: Background: Transglutaminase-crosslinked collagen gel (CHG) is a collagen product cross-linked with transglutaminase (TGase) that exhibits good thermal stability and has potential applications in functional food formulations. However, it remains unclear whether the gelation of CHG alters the metabolic fate of collagen-derived bioactive peptides in the gastrointestinal tract and their distribution within the body. Methods: This study investigated the retention of CHG in the gastrointestinal tract of male C57BL/6J mice, as well as its serum peptide levels and antioxidant activity. Results: Compared with unhydrolyzed (CNS) and hydrolyzed collagen (CHS) sols, CHG significantly prolonged gastric retention and slowed intestinal transit, while gastric contents exhibited larger particle sizes and a more sustained release of protein. title: Liquid metal interfaces for component mounting on kirigami stretchable substrates
authors: Takashi Sato; Wataru Iwasaki; Eiji Iwase
abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates liquid metal as an electrical interface material (LM-EIM) for mounting rigid electronic components on kirigami-based stretchable substrates. Kirigami structures impart high stretch tolerance to sheets made of materials with low stretchability through local bending and twisting. However, this advantage can be lost when rigid components are mounted using rigid EIMs, such as solder or conductive adhesive, because they mechanically constrain kirigami deformation and cause fracture at low strains. The LM-EIM itself exhibited high stretch tolerance, 24 and 35 times those of solder and adhesive, respectively. This highly deformable LM-EIM reduced constraints on kirigami deformation and suppressed fracture. Mounting with solder and adhesive reduced the substrate stretch tolerance to 32% and 36% of that without components, respectively. In contrast, mounting with the LM-EIM did not reduce the substrate stretch tolerance. The substrate fracture strain reached 3.99, corresponding to 1.1 times that without components. Finally, a resistor array maintained electrical connectivity up to a device strain of 2.0, while an LED array operated stably up to 1.5. This approach allows rigid, high-performance components to be integrated onto highly stretchable kirigami sheets without sacrificing their stretchability, enabling the development of high-performance, multifunctional stretchable electronics.

title: Kirigami‐Inspired Stretchable Silicon Solar Cell Modules as Portable Power Sources
authors: Yusheng Zhang; Chenyi Zhang; Pei Wang; Yetai Cheng; Qi Liang; Yonghuan Li; Zhengdong Wei; Huanyu Zhou; Xinyi Kong; Minghua Li; Yifan Wang; Zhishan Bo; Yuqiang Liu; Antonio Facchetti
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of photovoltaic modules into wearable electronic devices represents a pivotal advancement for enhancing portability and sustainability. Despite their high efficiency and stability, traditional silicon solar modules are brittle, preventing their applications in mechanically flexible and impact‐resistant wearable devices. Herein, we present a novel approach to deformable silicon solar cell modules of different sizes utilizing flexible kirigami‐structured substrates integrating commercial silicon cells, enabling durability against continuous deformations caused by body movements. For instance, our Module‐14‐7S2P, consisting of 14 silicon solar cells, exhibits a power output of 37.50 mW while maintaining > 95% power retention of its original power output after 5000 deformation cycles and > 94% power retention after 120 h of water immersion. Furthermore, upon deformation to a 13% strain, this module retains ∼80% of the initial power output, data supported by FEA simulations. Our study provides new possibilities for employing silicon solar cells in wearable applications, accelerating the adoption of sustainable and portable wearable electronic devices powered by solar energy.

title: Cross-Linking the Blue: Trends in Marine-Based Hydrogels
authors: Eylem Atak; Arita Dubnika; Maksims Melničuks; Karina Egle; Katja Klun; Ana Rotter
abstract: Marine-derived natural polymers have attracted increasing interest as sustainable, high-value biomaterials for hydrogel development, owing to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, and tunable physicochemical properties. This study maps publication retrieval and patent trends related to marine-derived biopolymers and hydrogel cross-linking technologies between 2000 and 2024, based on keyword searches of four bibliographic databases combining “marine”, the biopolymer name and “cross-linking”, with or without a specific cross-linking type, and individually screened patent records. Retrieval counts increased overall in all four databases with all search categories reaching their highest counts in 2020–2024, and the number of patents rose sharply in 2020–2024. Over the study period, alginate and chitosan were the most frequently retrieved algae- and animal-derived biopolymers in each database, while patents were concentrated in health and medical applications, with collagen represented in the highest number of patents. Among the cross-linking type terms, “chemical” returned the most records in every database, and no records were retrieved for the enzymatic cross-linking of most algae-derived biopolymers. Fucoidan, hyaluronic acid and carrageenan occupied an intermediate position, whereas ulvan, laminarin, agarose and chondroitin sulfate were rarely retrieved and had limited or no patent data. The main rankings were consistent across all four databases and the individually screened patent records showed similar temporal and biopolymer patterns. Based on these data, marine-derived polymers were classified into three development tiers, and the barriers and opportunities for their further development are discussed.

title: Solution-Processed Fiber-Shaped Wearable Electronics
authors: Si Hyeok YANG; Na Young LEE; Jin Woo CHOI
abstract: Fiber-shaped electronics provide a promising platform for wearable systems because of their intrinsic flexibility, lightweight structure, and compatibility with conventional textile processes. Solution processing is particularly attractive for fabricating such devices, as functional materials can be deposited onto fiber surfaces under relatively mild conditions using coating, printing, and related techniques. In this article, we review solution-processed fiber-shaped electronic devices for energy harvesting, storage, and utilization. Key challenges associated with material deposition, interface formation, mechanical durability, and electrical integration within textile structures are also discussed. Finally, we introduce the potential of ferroelectric nanotube-based composites as functional materials for multifunctional fiber-shaped devices, with particular emphasis on their future applications in wearable energy harvesting and sensing systems.

title: Efficient and Stable Red QLEDs via 4-TBP-Doped Hole Transport Layer Engineering
authors: Renjie Xiang; Tianshuo Zhang; Zurong Huang; Xinyu Wang; Ziming Zhou; Dexia Zhou; Zhaobing Tang; Siqi Jia; Jie Lin; Lishuang Wang; Xiao Wei Sun
abstract: Abstract The insufficient charge carrier mobility in the hole transport layer (HTL) and the energy level mismatch with the emissive layer have long been critical factors limiting the electroluminescence performance and carrier balance of quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). To address this issue, we employed 4-tert-butylpyridine (4-TBP) as a dopant in poly[(9,9-dioctylfluorenyl-2,7-diyl)-co-(4,4′-(N-(4-sec-butylphenyl)diphenylamine))] (TFB) as the HTL. By modulating the highest occupied molecular orbital energy level of TFB and enhancing the hole mobility, 4-TBP doping effectively reduces the hole injection barrier and suppresses interfacial charge accumulation. The optimized TFB:4-TBP HTL significantly improves hole injection efficiency in red QLEDs, leading to a decrease in turn-on voltage from 1.74 V to 1.65 V and an increase in external quantum efficiency (EQE) from 22.21 to 26.47%. Moreover, at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m–2, the QLED with the TFB:4-TBP HTL reaches a T95 operational lifetime of 11,708.67 h, which is 2.4 times longer than that of the undoped one. 1.22- and 1.37-fold improvements in EQEmax are obtained for green and blue QLEDs, respectively. This strategy demonstrates that 4-TBP doping, combined with interface engineering, provides an effective method to achieve efficient and stable hole transport, offering new insights for carrier balance control in solution-processed QLEDs.
